topic: Operating and securing a CockroachDB cluster
title: Operating and securing a CockroachDB cluster
brief: Operate a secure CockroachDB cluster with evidence about identity, range health and planned removal.
outcomes: Verify secure runtime identity, least privilege and tenant isolation
Diagnose under-replication and remove a node without losing the survival budget
entry: For security: general least privilege and trusted application/tenant ownership (RL104); the needed secure deployment and SQL object/session context is introduced locally. For node health/removal: also CockroachDB ranges (RL123), general rebalancing and the topology’s survival budget (RL109).

neighbours.RL123: Supplies range, lease and replica understanding before node health/removal work.
neighbours.RL109: Supplies movement and failure-headroom understanding before node health/removal work.

heading.title: Secure connections
heading.brief: Pin a secure owned deployment; explain certificate trust, server identity, client identity and SQL users without presenting insecure demo flags as production setup. Introduce the SQL database, schema, named objects and connection/session context needed for the permission tests.

heading.title: Permission boundaries
heading.brief: Choose and verify a native tenant boundary on the pinned release. Trace authenticated runtime identity and trustworthy shop selection through pooled connections; test permitted shop reads/writes, denied cross-shop reads/writes and attempted tenant-context spoofing, then expose the chosen mechanism’s bypass boundary. Check reporting read-only grants separately; table privileges alone do not establish tenant isolation.

heading.title: Range health under failure
heading.brief: After range/replica preparation in RL123 and rebalancing/survival-budget preparation in RL109, observe liveness, unavailable or under-replicated ranges and recovery work after node loss; connect metrics to the tested topology.

heading.title: Planned removal
heading.brief: With the same RL123/RL109 preparation, drain and decommission a node while tracking replica movement and headroom; verify the remaining cluster can still meet its stated failure goal.
